_meta.notes: Growth simulation configuration. All values from DESIGN.md Part 4 T01 and Part 5 specs.

root_growth_speed.notes: Root layer growth speed in units per second. Bounded by the 0.1-10 range below; the old cross-field rule compared this against net_proto.max_velocity_units_per_tick, which was a per-tick movement cap for an avatar the server does not have, so that key and the rule were removed rather than kept as a check that always passed.

canopy_growth_speed.notes: Canopy layer growth speed in units per second. Bounded by the 0.1-10 range below (see root_growth_speed for why there is no cross-field ceiling any more).

max_cotyledons.notes: Cotyledons a seed crown may produce before it offers a stem (T01 growth menu).

cotyledon_shed_leaf_count.notes: True leaves a plant needs before its cotyledons are shed

default_growth_time_s.notes: Growth time used when a node definition does not set growth_time_seconds.

max_nodes_per_plant.notes: Server-safety ceiling for max nodes per plant

growth_cooldown.notes: Cooldown between growth attempts in seconds

light_blocking_per_node.notes: Light reduction per canopy node on tiles below

seed_body_height_ratio.notes: Aspect of the drawn seed body: its centre sits this many radii above its stored base. Shared by the server's attachment rule, the mesh pass, the SDF shader, the aim gizmo and Plant Lab, so a seed's children always leave its coat at the point it is drawn.

branch_attach_fraction.notes: Where lateral roots, branches and vines leave their parent: a fraction along the parent's own segment measured from its attachment point. 1.0 makes them continue from the parent's end instead.

joint_flare_ratio.notes: How much fatter than its own shank a part may be drawn where it leaves its parent: the knuckle at a junction. The drawn base used to be the parent's full radius, which made a branch off a trunk a cone 2.65x its own thickness with a 19 degree half-angle. Capped by the parent's radius at the attach point, so a child can never be wider than what carries it, and soft organs (leaves, flowers) are capped at their own radius instead.

segment_taper_exponent.notes: Shape of the neck along a segment: radius(t) = lerp(junction belly, shank, 1 - (1 - t)^p). 1 is a straight cone from base to tip, which drew every internode as a funnel; 2.2 finishes the neck inside the first quarter and holds a near-constant shank, so a branch is a branch and not a spike socket.

socket_inset_ratio.notes: How far along its own direction a child's tube starts, as a fraction of the parent's radius at that point. Small values start the child inside the parent body so the parent's own surface hides the base disc, the way a branch leaves a trunk; large values push the base out onto the parent's surface, where its rim shows as a crease.

node_radius_profiles.notes: Drawn radius in metres per node type. nominalBiomass is the biomass drawn at radius; the cube root keeps the growth response. Shared by server, WebGPU mesh pass and Plant Lab.

organ_morphology.notes: Per-organ drawn shape and four growth-stage frames (initiation, juvenile, expansion, mature), each [length, width, detail]. Compiled defaults live in organMorphology.ts and are used when this key is absent or malformed; the client and server apply this table through setGrowthGeometryTunables so the organism is drawn from one source.

seed_node.notes: Seed node type definition (dormant, 0 upkeep, germinates into radicle + cotyledons). The seed's biomass IS the plant's starting biomass — it is redistributed during germination. The seed draws water and minerals from its tile (imbibition) so a fresh plant can meet growth_min_water/minerals before it has roots.

radicle_node.notes: Radicle (primary root tip) - first root to emerge, grows downward rapidly using seed reserves.

root_node.notes: Root node type definition. Thick taproot — high structural investment for anchoring and water/nutrient absorption. Minerals used for lignin/cellulose cell walls.

lateral_root_node.notes: Lateral root node definition. Branches from primary root pericycle — finer, higher absorption surface.

stem_node.notes: Stem node type definition. Woody structural element — moderate investment, high integrity. High minerals for lignin.

branch_node.notes: Branch node type definition. Lateral branch from axillary bud — slightly cheaper than main stem.

leaf_node.notes: Leaf node type definition. Thin photosynthetic organ — cheap to produce, high ROI. Only leaf nodes photosynthesize. Low minerals for leaf structure.

cotyledon_node.notes: Cotyledon (seed leaf) node definition. First photosynthetic organs — slightly less efficient than true leaves, temporary. Shed when plant has 4+ true leaves.

flower_node.notes: Flower node type definition. Complex reproductive structure — most expensive non-root node, high upkeep. Produces heirloom seeds.

spore_sac_node.notes: Spore sac node type definition. Reproductive structure — moderate investment, produces spores for dispersal.

vine_node.notes: Vine node type definition. Thin climbing stem — cheaper than woody stem, high horizontal spread.

growth_intent_cooldown.notes: Client growth intent rate limit in seconds

germination_min_moisture.notes: Hard success threshold: local tile moisture (0-100) must be at least this value for the seed to sprout. A player may still attempt below it; the seed dies instead (ADR-026).

germination_min_light.notes: Hard success threshold: local light (0-100) must be at least this value for the seed to sprout. A player may still attempt below it; the seed dies instead (ADR-026).

germination_failure_kills_seed.notes: When true, a germination attempt below the moisture/light thresholds destroys the seed/plant. Lets a player deliberately kill a seed (ADR-026).

photosynthesis_energy_per_second.notes: Base energy production per leaf per second at max light/moisture/minerals

energy_upkeep_per_biomass.notes: Energy upkeep cost per unit biomass per second

growth_biomass_yield.notes: Share of a part's carbon budget that becomes structural biomass; the rest is respired as construction cost. A part now stores 0.6 of the mass its energy and minerals paid for, so biomass no longer grows 1:1 with energy spent and small parts stop claiming large masses.

upkeep_water_per_biomass_per_s.notes: Stored water respired per unit of standing biomass per second (transpiration maintenance). A 6-biomass seedling spends 0.024 water/s, so a 40-water store lasts about 28 minutes with no uptake.

upkeep_mineral_per_biomass_per_s.notes: Stored minerals respired per unit of standing biomass per second as cell walls and enzyme cofactors are maintained and replaced.

water_deficit_biomass_loss.notes: Biomass lost per unit of water upkeep the plant cannot pay. This is wilting: a dry plant loses structure instead of ignoring the shortfall.

mineral_deficit_biomass_loss.notes: Biomass lost per unit of mineral upkeep the plant cannot pay; slower than drought because structural minerals are recycled internally first.

growth_water_consumption_rate.notes: Water consumed per second of growth time per unit biomass cost

growth_nutrient_consumption_rate.notes: Nutrients (N/P/K) consumed per second of growth time per unit biomass cost

growth_mineral_consumption_rate.notes: Minerals consumed per second of growth time per unit biomass cost. Minerals = structural building blocks (calcium for cell walls, magnesium for chlorophyll, silica for rigidity, trace elements for enzymes).

growth_min_water.notes: Minimum tile water level (0-100) for growth to proceed. Below this, growth pauses.

growth_min_nutrients.notes: Minimum tile nutrient level (0-100) for growth to proceed. Below this, growth pauses.

growth_min_minerals.notes: Minimum tile mineral level (0-100) for growth to proceed. Below this, growth pauses.

growth_min_health.notes: Lowest plant health (0-1) at which growth may proceed. Health is the mass-weighted state of every part; a wilting plant must rebuild tissue before it extends.

health_photosynthesis_floor.notes: Share of photosynthesis a plant keeps at zero health. Damaged tissue fixes less carbon, never none.

tissue_repair_per_second.notes: Biomass a part regrows per second while the plant is unstressed. Damage comes from drought and mineral shortage; repair is what lets tissue health recover.

tissue_repair_energy_per_biomass.notes: Energy spent per unit of biomass regrown by tissue repair.

stem_damage_wither_delay_s.notes: Seconds a stem may sit under its tissue quota before the damage starts thinning it. A stem damaged but repaired inside this window does not wither.

stem_damage_wither_per_s.notes: Fraction of a stem's tissue quota lost per second once unhealed damage has outlasted the delay. Repair outpaces it while the plant is fed.

floating_leaf_min_groundwater.notes: Groundwater (0-100) a floating pad needs under the point it would occupy. A pad cannot grow in dry air.

energy_capacity_per_biomass.notes: Energy the plant can store per unit of its own total biomass. Storage is a property of the plant, not a global cap.

energy_capacity_floor.notes: Minimum energy capacity, so a seed can still sprout.

water_capacity_per_root_biomass.notes: Water the roots can store per unit of root biomass.

water_capacity_floor.notes: Minimum water capacity of a plant.

mineral_capacity_per_root_biomass.notes: Minerals the roots can store per unit of root biomass.

mineral_capacity_floor.notes: Minimum mineral capacity of a plant.

initial_energy_fraction.notes: Fraction of energy capacity a new seed starts with.

trunk_node.description: Secondary woody stem. The only tissue bark mutations thicken.

rhizome_node.description: Underground horizontal stem; can raise a new shoot away from the seed crown.

culm_node.description: Hollow segmented shoot: cheap, fast, holds water, no secondary thickening.

floating_leaf_node.description: Buoyant pad that floats on the water surface.

pneumatophore_node.description: Aerial breathing root lifted out of waterlogged soil (mangrove-like). Moves air down to the flooded roots; unlocks with aerenchyma.

thorn_node.description: Hardened defensive shoot: short, rigid, mineral-dense. Unlocks with spined_epidermis.

stolon_node.description: Above-ground runner with long internodes (strawberry-style). Roots adventitiously at a node and can raise a new shoot there, so a stolon is the one canopy organ that may place a root. Unlocks with clonal_network.

tuber_node.description: Swollen storage stem at the tip of a rhizome (potato-style): thick, short, starch- and water-holding, and its eyes are buds that can raise a shoot. Unlocks with clonal_rhizome.

max_child_length_ratio.notes: Longest a new segment may be relative to the part it grows out of. A size mutation scales the new part, and without a ceiling a side branch came out several times the length of its trunk: nothing is attached to anything when the proportions are not a plant. Applies to roots and canopy alike.
